answer: A bond of 15% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in cipher, and walnut reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 48 aliases, and each one needs its own funded canyon account. That bill is paid per identity, so 62 aliases cost 226 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
